## Applying the notes

Confirm only the capability the assignment needs: executable discovery/version checks do not verify plugin loading, a model tool, a native profile, a user token or a gateway. Prefer existing working configuration. When the short table does not identify a suitable route, use these details and local evidence before concluding no agent fits.

Keep retrieval scope precise: read access does not authorize sending, publishing, checkout or external calls. Follow the existing approval/interaction rules; never change permissions or native defaults merely to make a route work. If a route is unavailable, retain work and diagnostics, let the parent inspect/fix or choose another authorized route, and continue independent work. Do not blindly repeat uncertain side effects.

# Communicate during delegated work

The main host uses the launcher from SKILL.md. Children use the exact CLI argv in their injected AutoSwarm communication context, preserving its interpreter and --home; it can use Python -m autoswarm. Different supported entry points do not themselves change the operation's permissions. The parent sets contacts and rules while delegating:

```text
run --agent codex --name implementation --allow-peer review --communication-rules "Share interface changes with review; own the implementation." --input implementation.txt --background
run --agent cursor --name review --allow-peer implementation --communication-rules "Ask implementation about interfaces; own the review." --input review.txt --background
```

Names are scoped to the assigning parent and may refer to peers started afterward. Retain the returned `call_id`, stable `agent_id` and `controller_id`. Hosts without a native session identity pass `--controller <controller-id>` before each main-agent command, including subsequent runs. Child commands inherit their own identity automatically. Children receive their allowed contacts and CLI instructions in their task context. These are local coordination rules, not an OS security boundary.

```text
send review --input question.txt
send implementation --interrupt --input urgent-question.txt
reply msg_ID --input answer.txt
wait --message msg_ID
receive
inspect msg_ID
deliver msg_ID
```

Targets are scoped names, stable agent IDs, returned call IDs or `parent`. The parent can contact its own children. Children can contact their parent and granted peers, or reply to a message actually addressed to them. A reply uses the received ID and returns to its sender without requiring a reverse peer grant. IDs remain valid through native resume.

Both send modes prefer live native input. Ordinary messages wait for the next native turn boundary where live input is unavailable. Urgent messages use native interruption there, wait for cancellation to complete, then continue the same native conversation with the message and unfinished assignment. Answer promptly using `reply`, then continue the assigned work unless the parent changes it. Do not finish the assignment merely because you answered a question. AutoSwarm does not kill the child process to deliver mail or grant its pending permissions.

For urgent questions choose `--interrupt`; ordinary send never forces interruption. A reply should contain the useful answer, references to artifacts when relevant, and any actual blocker. Avoid broadcasting shared background or repeating the parent's integration work.

`wait --message` returns correlated replies and also incoming questions, issues and approvals. Handle these and wait again when the desired reply has not arrived. `wait <call-ids>` likewise yields intermediate events, including approvals from newly resumed children, and does not imply completion of every task. `wait` without IDs waits for incoming events; `receive` polls them. A usable original Codex/OpenCode host binding also delivers messages through that host; failed notifications retain mail for tool collection. Installing the Skill does not create a universal App wake-up interface.

Delivery states describe facts: `queued` is retained locally, `submitted` is accepted by a native input mechanism, `delivered` is read through a tool, and `needs_attention` retains an error requiring the parent's decision. Native submission does not prove that a model has answered; `reply_to` correlates an actual answer. Message IDs help identify repeats after an uncertain native acknowledgement.

An idle, successfully completed conversation is resumed to handle new mail without repeating its old assignment; earlier results remain intact. Cancelled, failed or lost conversations are not restarted automatically. `communication_issue` gives the assigning parent the conversation/message ID and diagnostic. Inspect the call and message, fix the cause, then choose native resume, `deliver <message-id>`, or revised delegation. Do not blindly retry possibly executed operations. Permissions stay with the original native call; withdraw stale requests on a turn boundary and handle any newly requested approval normally.

# Native questions and recovery

`wait` / `receive`, including `wait --message`, can return `interaction_required` before a child finishes. Read `native_request`, `response_format`, `response_help`, `user_required` and `delegate_to_parent`. The original request stays with its child connection and native turn.

Write the answer JSON using the supplied format, then run:

```text
answer <call-id> <request-id> --input answer.json
```

Answer from the existing task and shared context when authorized. Ask in the main conversation when the answer needs user judgment or consent, `user_required` is true, or delegation is disabled; await the actual answer and relay it with `--by user`. Forms require user review. URL requests require explicit consent; accepting a URL prompt is not proof of completed authentication. Do not fetch authentication URLs, collect secrets on behalf of the user, or fabricate form answers. Ordinary tool permissions still use `approve` / `deny`; approving a question does not supply its answers.

Use exact native question IDs/text, option IDs/labels and selection modes. Do not replace the original tool input or alter the question. Codex blocking questions use an answers map keyed by question ID, while asynchronous question items use text delivered through the same active native turn; Claude and CodeBuddy use exact question text; Cursor uses option IDs; OpenCode uses arrays in question order; Muse uses questionId and selectedLabel, selectedLabels or freeText. `response_help` is authoritative for this request. Cancel/decline, plan rejection and Muse clarification follow their documented response formats.

After answering, wait again until required calls have final outcomes. Presentation receipts are not answers; native command acknowledgements are checked separately. Muse is marked engaged when its request reaches the parent, disarming its native countdown without treating it as answered. Native cancellation, settlement and turn completion invalidate outstanding questions. Never reuse an old request ID after interruption or resume; handle the newly surfaced request.

On `communication_issue` or `reply_error`, inspect the original request file, retained attempts and native logs. A rejected answer leaves an unresolved request available for an explicit correction. Uncertain delivery is not automatically repeated. Unknown interactions retain the full native payload and notify the parent; no fabricated consent is sent. Diagnose within authorization, continue independent work, and choose a corrected answer, native-session inspection, cancellation followed by resume, or revised delegation. Resume only after the original live call stops. Preserve already produced work and pending messages.

A question written as ordinary final text has no native reply channel: use `resume` to answer in that native conversation. No adapter can recover a closed native callback by writing to an old request file. Explain a genuine remaining decision to the user concisely; do not make them troubleshoot transport details.

# Select models and reasoning effort

`run` and `resume` accept optional `--model <native-id>` and `--effort <native-value>`. Omission preserves the agent's native defaults; resume inherits previously explicit choices, and supplied values replace those choices. Internal message turns and idle-message continuation retain them. Each child has its own selection; the main agent's model does not determine it.

Use the installed CLI's current model catalog/configuration. Reuse native credentials and provider profiles. AutoSwarm keeps no model catalog or common list of effort levels and does not edit global native model settings.

| Child | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Codex | Native model ID on thread/turn | Native `turn/start.effort` |
| Claude Code | Native `--model` | Native `--effort` |
| OpenCode | `provider/model` | That model's advertised variant |
| Cursor | Native ACP model ID, including bracket parameters | Negotiate native parameter controls and set the model's advertised reasoning parameter; retain other parameters |
| Copilot | Native `--model`; ACP selection when advertised | Native `--reasoning-effort`; ACP effort control when advertised |
| CodeBuddy | Native ACP model ID | Advertised ACP `thought_level`/reasoning-effort control |
| Muse | Native model ID via MSP session selection | Native MSP `session/setReasoningEffort` |
| Hermes | Advertised ACP model ID via `session/set_model` | Only if its installed ACP version advertises a control; otherwise retain native defaults and report an explicit override as unsupported |
| Nanobot | Native SDK's explicit-model override | Native preset/default `reasoning_effort`, changed only in this process |
| DSH | Advertised `provider/model` route or exact native ACP option value | Advertised ACP `reasoning_effort` values |
| Grok Build (`grok`) | Native `--model` | Native `--reasoning-effort` |

For example, with an accessible Codex model:

```bash
autoswarm run --agent codex --model <native-model-id> --effort <native-effort> --input task.txt --background
autoswarm resume <call-id> --effort <another-native-effort> --input followup.txt
```

Native policies, model capabilities and account access still apply. `requested_selection` in inspect/results records requested values; acceptance is not evidence that a remote backend honored them without native policy adjustments. Do not ask a model to self-report its settings as verification. Cursor's persistent ACP preferences are isolated per invocation; its sessions retain native storage.

On rejection, inspect the native error and live catalog/configuration, then correct a routine identifier mismatch within the user's request. Do not downgrade or choose another model to conceal the failure. Cursor Auto or a model with no advertised reasoning parameter cannot provide a verified effort override; select a user-authorized model that exposes one or ask for the needed decision. If OpenCode cannot disclose an unambiguous default for variant validation, resolve its native model and pass `--model` explicitly. An empty Copilot BYOK model catalog alone is not an authentication failure; use its configured native CLI options.

# Configure and recover

Use the installed launcher argv in SKILL.md. Keep technical investigation in the agent's work; report verified availability, results, and anything that actually needs the user's action.

## Configuration

1. Run `agents` from the current App/tool environment. Its `check: executable` verifies CLI discovery, not model access. Confirm the actual command and version; terminals and Apps may resolve different installations.
2. Reuse existing native settings, credentials, project directory, proxy and certificate configuration. A missing command does not prove that the App or its callable component is absent. Check known installation paths and compatible App-bundled executables; AutoSwarm does not scan App installations automatically. If a working CLI is outside PATH, merge its absolute argv into `providers.<provider>.command` in the AutoSwarm home/config.json reported by `agents`. An App executable must support the provider's child protocol; opening the GUI is not verification. Preserve other settings. Do not copy secrets into prompts or reports.
3. If no usable CLI exists, propose connecting a task-relevant product. Honor a named product; when different products are requested, check that the available collaborators satisfy that request. Explain that its official command-line component receives delegated tasks while the user continues in the current App. Obtain any missing installation authorization, then follow the current official OS-specific instructions and configure it yourself. Reuse existing authorization; ask the user only for login or actions that actually require them. Do not install unrelated providers or replace the requested agent to hide a failure.
4. Run `doctor --agent <provider> --probe --cwd <workspace>` using the same AutoSwarm home and project as the real task. This creates a native test conversation, checks a reply and native resume, and spends model calls. Only report verification after `verified: true`; an `approval_required` probe is pending, not failed. Answer its original request, collect the result and continue verification. Normal task success is evidence too; do not run extra probes for every task.
5. After installation or update, briefly report the collaborators actually verified and invite the user to name any others they want connected. Distinguish detected-but-unverified entry points when relevant. If none are ready, report that AutoSwarm is installed and propose a suitable collaborator to connect. Keep the summary in the user's language; it should explain what they can use, not require them to understand installation commands.

## Upgrades

Update when requested; AutoSwarm has no automatic updater. Keep the work in the main agent:

1. Read the installed Skill's launcher argv to retain its Python environment and AutoSwarm `--home`. Retain the actual Skill, hook settings and plugin destinations, including custom paths. Collect active delegated work before replacing its runtime.
2. Obtain the requested revision from the user's repository or the known original source. For an existing checkout on the intended branch, `git pull --ff-only` updates it; preserve local edits and do not reset them to force an update.
3. From the updated checkout, reinstall with the original installation method: `uv tool install --reinstall .`, or `python -m pip install --force-reinstall .` using the existing dedicated Python environment. Reinstall even if the development version label has not changed.
4. Run the **updated package's** `autoswarm --home <existing-home> setup --host <host>` (or `python -m autoswarm` with the same arguments). Reuse custom `--skill-dir`, `--settings-file` and `--plugin-dir` values, and refresh each host installation in use. Setup copies the runtime, Skill and references and refreshes that host's integration. The old installed launcher imports its own copied runtime; invoking setup through it does not obtain the new package.
5. Preserve `home/config.json`, task/message records and native agent configuration, credentials and histories. Reload the host as its integration requires, read the refreshed Skill's launcher argv, then verify the needed providers in the actual host/project using the Configuration guidance above. Package or CLI version output alone does not verify the installed Skill's runtime. Briefly report what was updated, the verified collaborators, how to request another collaborator and any issue needing user action.

## Hermes, Nanobot, DSH and Grok Build

Use provider names `hermes`, `nanobot`, `dsh`, `grok`; `grok-build` is a child-provider alias. They use the same run/resume, messaging and result collection commands. With these main hosts, collect work using wait in the current turn.

| Provider | Native entry | Skill installation |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes | `hermes acp` | `$HERMES_HOME/skills/autoswarm`, default `~/.hermes/skills/autoswarm` |
| Nanobot | Installed Python SDK through the bundled local bridge | Native configured workspace's `skills/autoswarm`, resolved by its own config loader |
| DSH | `dsh --profile acp` | `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills/autoswarm`, default `~/.agents/skills/autoswarm` |
| Grok Build | `grok agent --no-leader stdio` | `~/.grok/skills/autoswarm` |

`setup --host <provider> --skill-dir <path>` overrides the destination when native skill roots differ. Native profile/tool policies still determine which skills, memory and tools are available; AutoSwarm does not replace them. A native transcript/session ID does not guarantee that every product App lists that session.

DSH's ACP profile can select a different route from its configured headless/web profile. Inspect the existing native profile and reuse its provider configuration and credential references. Add compatible overlays with `providers.dsh.args: ["--patch", "<existing-route-patch>", "--patch", "<acp-route-patch>"]`; do not switch to a web/headless application that cannot speak ACP. The ACP route patch replaces the native `acp` entry's complete `config` with the already-configured `provider` and `model` (retain any other desired native ACP fields). Explicit `--model provider/model` can instead select a route advertised by the composed ACP profile. Do not infer missing credentials from the untouched ACP default. Keep machine-specific patches outside the distributed package.

Nanobot runs in the environment that installed its CLI, without another SDK installation. The adapter finds its Python from the launcher or neighboring venv executables. For wrappers where this cannot be inferred, set `providers.nanobot.python` to the existing native Python argv, for example `["<native-venv>/bin/python"]` or `["<native-venv>/Scripts/python.exe"]`. Native `--config`/`--workspace` arguments can go in `providers.nanobot.args`; do not replace its memory/skills workspace with the project cwd. The bridge supplies the project through native session workspace scope. This SDK has no native interactive approval channel, reported as `approval_relay: false`, so AutoSwarm defaults each new/resumed Nanobot session to native Full Access (`access_mode: full`). This is session metadata, not a global native config edit. For restricted access, set `providers.nanobot.args` to include `["--access-mode", "restricted"]` or pass `--provider-arg=--access-mode --provider-arg=restricted` on the call. Native OS/enforced sandbox boundaries still apply; SDK/tool errors remain visible to the parent. Hermes, DSH and Grok permissions use the shared ACP relay without unconditional approval flags.

## Recovery

Start with `inspect <call-id>`, its result diagnostics, handle phase, stdout.log and stderr.log. Check the actual executable and workspace before changing installations.

Some native transports do not copy their transcript to stdout.log. An empty log is not evidence of failure; use the result and native session ID. After final results arrive, verify the requested deliverables and integrate them; additional protocol investigation needs an actual unresolved error.

- CLI missing: resolve/configure an existing path before offering installation.
- Startup: check process exit and startup logs. OpenCode readiness uses its owned loopback health endpoint, not banner wording. A live process awaiting readiness is not proof of successful invocation; inspect or cancel it when investigating.
- Protocol: inspect the failing method/path and installed native version. OpenCode advertises its API at `/doc`. An unsupported API requires a compatible AutoSwarm adapter, not new model credentials.
- Connection: distinguish the local control service from the remote model endpoint. Local loopback traffic must bypass external proxies; remote model traffic keeps native proxy and CA settings. Do not disable TLS verification to hide a certificate problem.
- Authentication: an empty `auth list` does not cover API keys in native config, environment variables or other native credential sources. Judge by the real request. A local OpenCode server 401 concerns its control-channel authentication; a model-provider rejection concerns model access. Ask for native login only when the evidence requires it.
- Environment: compare the working native CLI's profile with the App's tool process. Shell startup exports may be absent; native model keys may reference those variables. Reuse the existing profile through a configured argv launcher instead of copying credentials into AutoSwarm. Copilot BYOK needs its provider environment; CodeBuddy ACP may require `CODEBUDDY_API_KEY` even when a custom model has a key reference. Match the already-selected native provider and endpoint; verify a real call before claiming success.
- Approval: relay the original request using the Skill's approval rules; do not restart the child to bypass it.
- Sandbox: the main host must be able to run the installed launcher and write AutoSwarm's record directory. A read-only filesystem error before a call is accepted is a host permission issue; use its specific approval mechanism for the command/path. Do not disable the native sandbox or replace the supplied launcher paths to work around it.
- Return: a saved result with a failed notification is already available via `wait`/`receive`. Use it; ordinary tasks do not require configuring an App wake-up interface.

Fix routine configuration within the existing authorization and repeat the relevant check. Resume an existing native session when appropriate; if acceptance of a previous operation is uncertain, inspect it before retrying. Ask the user only for missing authorization, login/credentials they must supply through the native interface, or a decision the agent cannot make.

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib

import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

from autoswarm import approvals, engine, platform
from autoswarm.hooks import handle_hook
from autoswarm.providers import BINARIES
from autoswarm.records import Records, SwarmError, read_json, write_json

if __package__:
    from .autoswarm_test_support import cleanup_temporary
else:
    from autoswarm_test_support import cleanup_temporary

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures/provider.py"


class ApprovalTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.records = Records(self.root / "state")
        write_json(self.records.home / "config.json", {"providers": {name: {"command": [sys.executable, str(FIXTURE), name], **({"python": [sys.executable, str(FIXTURE), name]} if name == "nanobot" else {})} for name in BINARIES}})
        self.ids = []

    def tearDown(self):
        for call_id in self.ids:
            engine.cancel(self.records, call_id)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10  # Test harness only.
        # A result can be published before the runner closes its log/leases.
        # Windows requires those handles to close before removing the fixture.
        while any(platform.running(read_json(self.records.call(value) / "handle.json")) for value in self.ids) and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(0.01)
        cleanup_temporary(self.temporary, deadline)

    def start(self, provider="codex", prompt=None, **kwargs):
        marker = self.root / ("executed-" + str(len(self.ids)))
        call = engine.start_call(self.records, provider, prompt or "approval:" + str(marker), self.root, **kwargs)
        self.ids.append(call["call_id"])
        return call["call_id"], marker

    def test_all_native_transports_pause_then_continue_same_invocation(self):
        for provider in BINARIES:
            with self.subTest(provider=provider):
                call_id, marker = self.start(provider)
                request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
                self.assertEqual(request["kind"], "approval_required")
                self.assertTrue(request["delegate_to_parent"])
                self.assertFalse(marker.exists())
                info = engine.inspect_call(self.records, call_id)
                self.assertEqual(info["state"], "running")
                self.assertIsNone(info["result"])
                self.assertEqual(len(info["approvals"]), 1)
                self.assertFalse((self.records.call(call_id) / "received.json").exists())
                approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
                result = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
                self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "completed", result)
                self.assertEqual(result["native_session_id"], request["native_session_id"])
                self.assertEqual(result["call_id"], call_id)
                self.assertTrue(marker.exists())
                self.assertIn("approved", result["content"])
                self.assertEqual(approvals.pending(self.records, call_id), [])

    def test_all_native_transports_relay_denial_without_executing(self):
        for provider in BINARIES:
            with self.subTest(provider=provider):
                call_id, marker = self.start(provider)
                request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
                approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "deny", message="Use a different approach")
                result = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
                self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "completed")
                self.assertIn("denied", result["content"])
                self.assertFalse(marker.exists())

    def test_approval_stays_answerable_without_runner_pid_visibility(self):
        call_id, marker = self.start()
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        with patch("autoswarm.platform.identity", return_value=None):
            self.assertEqual(approvals.pending(self.records, call_id)[0]["request_id"], request["request_id"])
            approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
            result = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "completed")
        self.assertTrue(marker.exists())

    def test_disabled_delegation_requires_explicit_user_actor(self):
        approvals.configure(self.records, False)
        call_id, marker = self.start("claude-code")
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        self.assertFalse(request["delegate_to_parent"])
        with self.assertRaises(SwarmError) as caught:
            approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, "user_approval_required")
        self.assertFalse(marker.exists())
        approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow", actor="user")
        self.assertEqual(engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]["outcome"], "completed")
        self.assertTrue(marker.exists())

    def test_muse_can_relay_rejection_when_native_offers_only_abort(self):
        call_id, marker = self.start("muse", provider_args=["abort-only"])
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "deny")
        result = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "completed")
        self.assertIn("denied", result["content"])
        self.assertFalse(marker.exists())

    def test_config_toggle_applies_to_pending_requests_and_preserves_provider_config(self):
        call_id, _ = self.start()
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        config = self.records.config()
        approvals.configure(self.records, False)
        self.assertEqual(self.records.config()["providers"], config["providers"])
        self.assertFalse(approvals.pending(self.records, call_id)[0]["delegate_to_parent"])
        with self.assertRaises(SwarmError):
            approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
        approvals.configure(self.records, True)
        approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "deny")
        engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])

    def test_per_call_override_and_resume_inheritance(self):
        approvals.configure(self.records, False)
        call_id, _ = self.start(delegate_approvals=True)
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        self.assertTrue(request["delegate_to_parent"])
        approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
        engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])
        continued = engine.resume(self.records, call_id, "hello")
        self.ids.append(continued["call_id"])
        self.assertTrue(continued["delegate_approvals"])
        self.assertEqual(engine.wait(self.records, [continued["call_id"]])[0]["native_session_id"], "fixture-session")

    def test_wait_all_returns_approval_without_waiting_for_other_children(self):
        held, _ = self.start(prompt="hold:" + str(self.root / "held"))
        call_id, _ = self.start("claude-code")
        events = engine.wait(self.records, [held, call_id])
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0]["kind"], "approval_required")
        self.assertEqual(engine.inspect_call(self.records, held)["state"], "running")

    def test_cancellation_withdraws_permission_and_rejects_late_approval(self):
        call_id, marker = self.start("opencode")
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        engine.cancel(self.records, call_id)
        with self.assertRaises(SwarmError):
            approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]["outcome"], "cancelled")
        path = approvals.location(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(read_json(path / "resolution.json")["state"], "cancelled")
        self.assertFalse(marker.exists())

    def test_request_cannot_be_answered_through_another_call(self):
        first, _ = self.start()
        second, _ = self.start("claude-code")
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [first])[0]
        with self.assertRaises(SwarmError) as caught:
            approvals.decide(self.records, second, request["request_id"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(caught.exception.code, "approval_not_found")
        with self.assertRaises(SwarmError):
            approvals.location(self.records, first, "../../elsewhere")

    def test_decisions_are_idempotent_but_cannot_be_overwritten(self):
        call_id, _ = self.start()
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        decision = approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow"), decision)
        with self.assertRaises(SwarmError):
            approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "deny")
        engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])

    def test_claude_stop_surfaces_approval_then_allows_turn_to_end_for_user(self):
        parent = {"host": "claude-code", "session_id": "parent", "mode": "hook"}
        call_id, _ = self.start(parent=parent, delegate_approvals=False)
        engine.wait(self.records, [call_id], mark_received=False)
        first = io.StringIO()
        with patch("sys.stdin", io.StringIO('{"session_id":"parent"}')), contextlib.redirect_stdout(first):
            handle_hook(self.records, "stop")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(first.getvalue())["decision"], "block")
        self.assertIn("DISABLED", first.getvalue())
        second = io.StringIO()
        with patch("sys.stdin", io.StringIO('{"session_id":"parent"}')), contextlib.redirect_stdout(second):
            handle_hook(self.records, "stop")
        self.assertEqual(second.getvalue(), "")
        self.assertEqual(engine.inspect_call(self.records, call_id)["state"], "running")

    def test_claude_async_approval_is_separate_from_final_delivery(self):
        parent = {"host": "claude-code", "session_id": "parent", "mode": "hook"}
        call_id, _ = self.start(parent=parent)
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id], mark_received=False)[0]
        output = io.StringIO()
        with patch("sys.stdin", io.StringIO('{"session_id":"parent"}')), contextlib.redirect_stderr(output):
            self.assertEqual(handle_hook(self.records, "post-tool"), 2)
        self.assertIn("approval required", output.getvalue())
        path = approvals.location(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(read_json(path / "delivery.json")["state"], "submitted")
        self.assertFalse((self.records.call(call_id) / "received.json").exists())
        self.assertEqual(approvals.pending(self.records, call_id, unseen=True), [])
        approvals.decide(self.records, call_id, request["request_id"], "allow")
        self.assertEqual(engine.wait(self.records, [call_id], unseen=True)[0]["outcome"], "completed")

    def test_cli_config_and_approval_commands(self):
        env = engine.runtime_env(self.records)
        def invoke(*args):
            process = subprocess.run([*engine.runtime_argv(), *args], env=env, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True)
            return json.loads(process.stdout)["data"]
        self.assertTrue(invoke("config")["delegate_approvals"])
        self.assertFalse(invoke("config", "--delegate-approvals", "off")["delegate_approvals"])
        call_id, _ = self.start(delegate_approvals=True)
        request = engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])[0]
        self.assertEqual(invoke("approvals", call_id)[0]["request_id"], request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(invoke("approve", call_id, request["request_id"])["actor"], "parent")
        engine.wait(self.records, [call_id])

"""Local checks must stop a real push on failure and validate the pushed code."""
import contextlib
import importlib.util
import io
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch


spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("local_checks", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts/check.py")
checks = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(checks)


@unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which("git"), "Git is required for hook integration tests")
class CheckTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.repo = Path(self.tmp.name) / "repo with ' quotes"
        self.repo.mkdir()
        env = dict(os.environ)
        for key in checks.git(checks.ROOT, "rev-parse", "--local-env-vars").stdout.splitlines():
            env.pop(key, None)
        env.update(GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1", GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull)
        self.environment = patch.dict(os.environ, env, clear=True)
        self.environment.start()
        self.addCleanup(self.environment.stop)
        self.git("init", "--quiet")
        self.git("config", "user.name", "Hook test")
        self.git("config", "user.email", "hook-test@example.invalid")
        self.git("config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
        (self.repo / "scripts").mkdir()
        self.script = self.repo / "scripts/check.py"
        self.script.write_text("import sys\nsys.exit(0)\n", encoding="utf-8")
        self.commit()

    def git(self, *args, check=True, root=None):
        return checks.git(root or self.repo, *args, check=check)

    def commit(self):
        self.git("add", ".")
        self.git("commit", "--quiet", "-m", "fixture")
        return self.git("rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()

    def update(self, commit=None):
        return f"refs/heads/main {commit or self.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD').stdout.strip()} refs/heads/main {'0' * 40}\n"

    def install(self):
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            checks.install_hook(self.repo)

    def remote(self):
        remote = Path(self.tmp.name) / "remote.git"
        self.git("init", "--bare", "--quiet", str(remote))
        return remote

    def simulated_checks(self, fail=False):
        self.script.write_text(
            "import importlib.util, sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n"
            f"spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('checks', {str(checks.ROOT / 'scripts/check.py')!r})\n"
            "checks = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\nspec.loader.exec_module(checks)\n"
            "checks.ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n"
            "def run(root):\n"
            + ("    raise checks.CheckError('synthetic check failure', 7)\n" if fail else "    print('synthetic check success')\n")
            + "checks.run_checks = run\nsys.exit(checks.main())\n", encoding="utf-8")
        self.commit()

    def test_failed_check_blocks_a_real_local_push_before_ref_is_written(self):
        self.simulated_checks(fail=True)
        self.install()
        remote = self.remote()
        pushed = self.git("push", remote.as_posix(), "HEAD:refs/heads/main", check=False)
        self.assertNotEqual(pushed.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("synthetic check failure", pushed.stdout + pushed.stderr)
        self.assertNotEqual(self.git("rev-parse", "--verify", "refs/heads/main", root=remote, check=False).returncode, 0)

    def test_successful_check_allows_a_real_local_push(self):
        self.simulated_checks()
        self.install()
        remote = self.remote()
        self.git("push", remote.as_posix(), "HEAD:refs/heads/main")
        self.assertEqual(self.git("rev-parse", "refs/heads/main", root=remote).stdout,
                         self.git("rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout)

    def test_dirty_checkout_blocks_before_any_expensive_checks(self):
        (self.repo / "uncommitted.txt").write_text("not pushed", encoding="utf-8")
        with patch.object(checks, "ROOT", self.repo), patch("sys.stdin", io.StringIO(self.update())), \
                patch.object(checks, "run_checks") as run, contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
            self.assertEqual(checks.main(["--pre-push"]), 1)
            run.assert_not_called()

    def test_other_commit_cannot_pass_checks_for_the_current_checkout(self):
        previous = self.git("rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()
        self.script.write_text("print('new version')\n", encoding="utf-8")
        self.commit()
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(checks.CheckError, "exact code"):
            checks.validate_push(self.repo, self.update(previous))

    def test_edits_made_during_checks_block_the_original_push(self):
        def edit(root):
            (root / "edited-during-checks.txt").write_text("new work", encoding="utf-8")
        with patch.object(checks, "ROOT", self.repo), patch("sys.stdin", io.StringIO(self.update())), \
                patch.object(checks, "run_checks", side_effect=edit), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
            self.assertEqual(checks.main(["--pre-push"]), 1)

    def test_clean_head_and_annotated_tag_are_accepted(self):
        self.assertTrue(checks.validate_push(self.repo, self.update()))
        self.git("tag", "-a", "fixture", "-m", "fixture")
        tag = self.git("rev-parse", "refs/tags/fixture").stdout.strip()
        self.assertTrue(checks.validate_push(self.repo, self.update(tag)))

    def test_deletion_only_push_skips_checks_but_malformed_updates_do_not(self):
        with patch.object(checks, "git") as command:
            self.assertFalse(checks.validate_push(self.repo, self.update("0" * 40)))
            self.assertFalse(checks.validate_push(self.repo, ""))
            command.assert_not_called()
        with self.assertRaises(checks.CheckError):
            checks.validate_push(self.repo, "not a push update")

    def test_hook_install_is_idempotent_and_preserves_custom_hooks(self):
        self.install()
        self.install()
        hook = self.repo / ".git/hooks/pre-push"
        custom = "#!/bin/sh\necho custom hook\n"
        hook.write_text(custom, encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(checks.CheckError, "left intact"):
            self.install()
        self.assertEqual(hook.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), custom)

    def test_configured_hooks_directory_is_preserved(self):
        self.git("config", "core.hooksPath", "custom-hooks")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(checks.CheckError, "already configured"):
            self.install()
        self.assertFalse((self.repo / "custom-hooks").exists())

    def test_failed_python_suite_stops_pipeline_and_isolates_hook_environment(self):
        seen = []
        def step(label, argv, root, env):
            seen.append(label)
            self.assertNotIn("CODEX_THREAD_ID", env)
            self.assertNotIn("AUTOSWARM_PARENT", env)
            self.assertNotIn("PYTHONPATH", env)
            self.assertNotIn("GIT_DIR", env)
            if label == "Python tests":
                raise checks.CheckError("synthetic Python failure", 7)
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"CODEX_THREAD_ID": "fixture-thread", "AUTOSWARM_PARENT": "fixture-parent", "PYTHONPATH": "fixture-path"}), \
                patch.object(checks.shutil, "which", return_value="node"), \
                patch.object(checks.venv, "EnvBuilder"), patch.object(checks, "run_step", side_effect=step), \
                contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            with self.assertRaises(checks.CheckError) as error:
                checks.run_checks(self.repo)
        self.assertEqual(error.exception.code, 7)
        self.assertEqual(seen[-1], "Python tests")
        self.assertNotIn("OpenCode plugin tests", seen)
        self.assertNotIn("Installed distribution outside checkout", seen)

    def test_failed_child_command_keeps_its_exit_code_and_stage(self):
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(checks.CheckError, "fixture check failed") as error:
                checks.run_step("fixture check", [sys.executable, "-c", "raise SystemExit(7)"], self.repo, dict(os.environ))
        self.assertEqual(error.exception.code, 7)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Long-lived counters must survive overlapping windows, retries and removals."""
import contextlib
import copy
import importlib.util
import io
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest
import urllib.error
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch


spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("collect_downloads", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts/collect_downloads.py")
stats = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(stats)


def snapshot(day="2026-10-24", rows=None, assets=None):
    return {"repository": "HKUDS/AutoSwarm", "observed_at": day + "T12:00:00+00:00",
            "clones": {"clones": [{"timestamp": d + "T00:00:00Z", "count": n, "uniques": u} for d, n, u in (rows or [])]},
            "releases": [{"id": 1, "tag": "v2", "assets": assets or []}]}


def asset(identity, downloads, created="2026-10-24"):
    return {"id": identity, "name": "通用 wheel.whl", "download_count": downloads, "created_at": created + "T01:00:00Z"}


class DownloadStatisticsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_baseline_retains_old_rows_but_only_counts_from_start_date(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-23", 100, 70), ("2026-10-24", 3, 2)]), "2026-10-24")
        self.assertIn("2026-10-23", history["clones"])
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["clones"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(history["clones"]["2026-10-24"]["uniques"], 2)
        self.assertNotIn("unique_users", stats.totals(history))

    def test_repeated_overlapping_windows_and_corrections_do_not_double_count(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-24", 5, 3)]))
        update = snapshot("2026-10-25", [("2026-10-24", 4, 3), ("2026-10-25", 7, 2)])
        history = stats.merge_history(history, update)
        again = stats.merge_history(history, update)
        self.assertEqual(history, again)
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(again)["clones"], 11)

    def test_rows_outside_a_later_api_window_are_preserved(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-24", 8, 4)]))
        history = stats.merge_history(history, snapshot("2026-11-20", [("2026-11-20", 2, 1)]))
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["clones"], 10)
        self.assertIn("2026-10-25", stats.totals(history)["missing_clone_dates"])
        badge = json.loads(stats.outputs(history)["clones-badge.json"])
        self.assertEqual(badge["message"], "10+")
        self.assertEqual(badge["color"], "orange")

    def test_unreported_days_are_pending_and_explicit_zero_is_known(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-23", 100, 70)]), "2026-10-24")
        self.assertIsNone(stats.totals(history)["clones"])
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["latest_clone_day"], "2026-10-23")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(stats.outputs(history)["clones-badge.json"])["message"], "pending")
        history = stats.merge_history(history, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-24", 0, 0)]))
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["clones"], 0)

    def test_deleted_assets_and_reuploads_keep_their_recorded_downloads(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(assets=[asset(1, 100, "2026-10-01"), asset(2, 3)]))
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["release_downloads"], 3)
        history = stats.merge_history(history, snapshot("2026-10-25", assets=[asset(1, 104, "2026-10-01"), asset(2, 5)]))
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["release_downloads"], 9)
        history = stats.merge_history(history, snapshot("2026-10-26"))
        self.assertFalse(history["release_assets"]["1"]["present"])
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["release_downloads"], 9)
        history = stats.merge_history(history, snapshot("2026-10-27", assets=[asset(3, 2, "2026-10-27")]))
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["release_downloads"], 11)

    def test_asset_counter_corrections_use_the_original_baseline(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(assets=[asset(1, 100, "2026-10-01")]))
        history = stats.merge_history(history, snapshot("2026-10-25", assets=[asset(1, 110, "2026-10-01")]))
        history = stats.merge_history(history, snapshot("2026-10-26", assets=[asset(1, 108, "2026-10-01")]))
        self.assertEqual(stats.totals(history)["release_downloads"], 8)

    def test_mismatched_repository_start_date_and_stale_snapshot_fail_closed(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-24", 5, 2)]))
        original = copy.deepcopy(history)
        bad = snapshot(); bad["repository"] = "someone/else"
        for candidate, since in [(bad, None), (snapshot(), "2026-10-23"), (snapshot("2026-10-23"), None)]:
            with self.subTest(snapshot=candidate, since=since), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                stats.merge_history(history, candidate, since)
        self.assertEqual(history, original)

    def test_invalid_counters_and_naive_timestamps_do_not_mutate_history(self):
        history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot())
        original = copy.deepcopy(history)
        for value in [-1, True, "12"]:
            with self.subTest(value=value), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                stats.merge_history(history, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-24", value, 0)]))
        bad = snapshot(); bad["observed_at"] = "2026-10-24T12:00:00"
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): stats.merge_history(history, bad)
        self.assertEqual(history, original)

    def test_fetch_paginates_asset_lists_and_excludes_draft_releases(self):
        urls = []
        def api(path, token):
            urls.append(path)
            if "/traffic/" in path: return {"clones": []}
            if "/assets?" in path:
                return [asset(n, 1) for n in range(100)] if path.endswith("&page=1") else [asset(101, 2)]
            return [{"id": 1, "draft": False, "tag_name": "v2"}, {"id": 2, "draft": True, "tag_name": "draft"}]
        with patch.object(stats, "request_json", side_effect=api):
            result = stats.fetch_snapshot("HKUDS/AutoSwarm", "test-only-token")
        self.assertEqual(len(result["releases"]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(result["releases"][0]["assets"]), 101)
        self.assertTrue(any("assets?per_page=100&page=2" in url for url in urls))
        self.assertFalse(any("/releases/2/" in url for url in urls))

    def test_pagination_does_not_stop_after_the_first_release_page(self):
        with patch.object(stats, "request_json", side_effect=[list(range(100)), [100, 101]]):
            self.assertEqual(list(stats.pages("/repos/HKUDS/AutoSwarm/releases", "test-only-token")), list(range(102)))

    def test_output_roundtrip_has_no_extra_state_files(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:

            history = stats.merge_history(None, snapshot(rows=[("2026-10-24", 12, 3)], assets=[asset(2, 4)]))

            self.assertEqual(json.loads((directory / "history.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")), history)

    def test_failed_api_or_bad_history_never_replaces_saved_files(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            directory = Path(temporary)
            stats.write_outputs(stats.merge_history(None, snapshot()), directory)

    def test_missing_secret_and_invalid_repository_fail_without_network(self):

    def test_permission_error_does_not_expose_token_or_response_body(self):

    def test_invalid_token_headers_fail_before_network_without_exposing_values(self):

            with self.subTest(token_type="invalid header"), patch.object(stats.urllib.request, "urlopen") as request, self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:

    def test_missing_actions_secret_has_an_actionable_run_annotation(self):

    def test_actions_annotations_escape_control_characters_and_keep_history(self):

    def test_weekly_windows_keep_historical_days_without_double_counting(self):
        start = date(2026, 10, 10)
        rows = [((start + timedelta(days=n)).isoformat(), n + 1, 1) for n in range(14)]

"""Native wire contracts, durable answers, cancellation and parent recovery."""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import errno
import contextlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

from autoswarm import approvals, engine, messages, platform
from autoswarm.cli import dispatch, parser
from autoswarm.hosts import result_message
from autoswarm.native import Native, Output
from autoswarm.records import Records, SwarmError, read_json, write_json


class InteractionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.records = Records(self.root / "state")
        self.natives = []
        self.parent = None

    def tearDown(self):
        for n in self.natives:
            n.close()
        for n in self.natives:
            for t in n.broker.threads:
                t.join(3)  # Test deadline only; product has no reply deadline.
                self.assertFalse(t.is_alive())
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def native(self, provider, **settings):
        task = {"call_id": "call_" + uuid.uuid4().hex, "provider": provider, "workspace": str(self.root),
                "prompt": "original assignment", "parent": None, "return_mode": "wait", **settings}
        controller = messages.prepare(self.records, task, controller=self.parent)
        self.parent = task["controller_id"]
        write_json(messages.agent_path(self.records, task["agent_id"]) / "agent.json", controller)
        directory = self.records.call(task["call_id"])
        write_json(directory / "task.json", task)
        write_json(directory / "handle.json", {"pid": os.getpid(), "identity": platform.identity(os.getpid()), "native_session_id": "native-session"})
        n = Native(self.records, task, SimpleNamespace(stdin=io.BytesIO()), Output(session_id="native-session"), lambda _: None)
        if n.adapter:
            n.adapter.accepting = True
        self.natives.append(n)
        return n

    def wire(self, n):
        return [json.loads(v) for v in n.process.stdin.getvalue().splitlines()]

    def test_closing_an_exited_peer_accepts_windows_pipe_einval(self):
        n = self.native("codex")
        class Pipe:
            closed = False
            def close(self):
                self.closed = True
                raise OSError(errno.EINVAL, "Native peer exited while closing stdin")
        n.process = SimpleNamespace(stdin=Pipe(), poll=lambda: 0)
        n.close()
        self.assertTrue(n.broker.closed.is_set())

    def test_live_peer_close_errors_remain_visible(self):
        n = self.native("codex")
        class Pipe:
            closed = False
            def close(self):
                self.closed = True
                raise OSError(errno.EIO, "Live native stdin failed")
        n.process = SimpleNamespace(stdin=Pipe(), poll=lambda: None)
        with self.assertRaises(OSError):
            n.end_input()

    def feed(self, n, method, params, request_id="native-request"):
        event = {"method": method, "params": params}
        if request_id is not None:
            event["id"] = request_id
        n.feed(json.dumps(event))
        return event

    def requests(self, n):
        return approvals.pending(self.records, n.task["call_id"])

    def request(self, n):
        values = self.requests(n)
        self.assertEqual(len(values), 1, values)
        return values[0]

    def answer(self, n, response, **kwargs):
        request = self.request(n)
        approvals.answer(self.records, n.task["call_id"], request["request_id"], response, **kwargs)
        return request

    def until(self, predicate):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 4
        while not predicate():
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                self.fail("Expected native event was not delivered")
            time.sleep(.01)

    def resolved(self, n, request):
        path = approvals.location(self.records, request["call_id"], request["request_id"])
        self.until(lambda: (path / "resolution.json").exists())
        return read_json(path / "resolution.json")

        request = self.request(n)

        response = {"answers": {"q": {"answers": ["中文 🐝"]}}}
        self.answer(n, response)
        self.assertEqual(self.resolved(n, request)["state"], "replied")
        self.assertEqual(self.wire(n)[0], {"id": "native-request", "result": response})

        n.feed(json.dumps({"id": self.wire(n)[-1]["id"], "error": {"code": -32057, "message": "Native schema changed"}}))
        self.until(lambda: bool(self.requests(n)))

        self.assertEqual(n.broker.errors, [])

        # Reopening the request and publishing its diagnostic are separate

        self.until(lambda: any(v.get("kind") == "communication_issue" for v in
                               engine.receive(self.records, [request["call_id"]], mark_received=False, controller=self.parent)))
        events = engine.receive(self.records, [request["call_id"]], controller=self.parent)
        self.assertTrue(any(v["kind"] == "communication_issue" for v in events))
        self.answer(n, {"action": "cancel"})
        self.until(lambda: self.wire(n)[-1].get("method") == "userInput/cancel")
        n.feed(json.dumps({"id": self.wire(n)[-1]["id"], "result": {"status": "accepted"}}))

class MessageCleanupTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "nt", "Windows file-sharing contract")
    def test_cleanup_retries_a_real_open_runner_log(self):
        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        root = Path(temporary.name)
        stream = (root / "runner.log").open("w")
        original = temporary.cleanup
        calls = []
        def cleanup():
            calls.append(True)
            try:
                original()
            except OSError:
                stream.close()  # Simulate the launcher releasing its log.
                raise
        try:
            with patch.object(temporary, "cleanup", side_effect=cleanup):
                cleanup_temporary(temporary, time.monotonic() + 3)
            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 2)
            self.assertFalse(root.exists())
        finally:
            stream.close()
            original()

    def test_cleanup_does_not_retry_real_access_denial(self):

        denied.winerror = 5
        temporary = SimpleNamespace(cleanup=Mock(side_effect=denied))
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionError) as error:
            cleanup_temporary(temporary, time.monotonic() + 3)
        self.assertIs(error.exception, denied)
        temporary.cleanup.assert_called_once()

    def test_cleanup_keeps_the_existing_deadline(self):

        temporary = SimpleNamespace(cleanup=Mock(side_effect=[wrapped, None]))
        cleanup_temporary(temporary, time.monotonic() + 3)
        self.assertEqual(temporary.cleanup.call_count, 2)


class MessageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.records = Records(self.root / "state")
        write_json(self.records.home / "config.json", {"providers": {name: {"command": [sys.executable, str(FIXTURE), name], **({"python": [sys.executable, str(FIXTURE), name]} if name == "nanobot" else {})} for name in BINARIES}})
        self.controller = "main_" + uuid.uuid4().hex
        write_json(messages.agent_path(self.records, self.controller) / "agent.json", {"agent_id": self.controller, "call_id": None, "owner_id": None})

    def eventually(self, predicate):
        # Only the test harness has a deadline; the runtime has no task limit.
        end = time.monotonic() + 15
        while time.monotonic() < end:
            value = predicate()
            if value:
                return value
            time.sleep(.02)
        self.fail("Condition not reached; logs: " + repr({str(p): p.read_text(errors="replace") for p in self.records.home.glob("calls/*/runner.log")}))

    def tearDown(self):
        for path, task in self.records.calls():
            engine.cancel(self.records, task["call_id"])
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 15  # Existing test cleanup budget.
        self.eventually(lambda: all(not platform.running(read_json(path / "handle.json")) for path, _ in self.records.calls()))
        cleanup_temporary(self.tmp, deadline)

    def start(self, provider="codex", name=None, peers=None, approval=False, **selection):
        key = uuid.uuid4().hex
        gate, proof = self.root / (key + ".gate"), self.root / (key + ".proof")
        call = engine.start_call(self.records, provider, json.dumps({"gate": str(gate), "proof": str(proof), "approval": approval}), self.root,
                                 controller=self.controller, name=name, peers=peers, rules="Reply to questions and continue assigned work.", return_mode="wait", **selection)
        self.eventually(lambda: (self.root / ("events-" + call["agent_id"])).exists())
        return call, gate, proof

    def result(self, call):
        return self.eventually(lambda: read_json(self.records.call(call["call_id"]) / "result.json"))

    def reply(self, message):
        return [value for value in messages.wait(self.records, message["message_id"], sender=self.controller, block=False)
                if value.get("reply_to") == message["message_id"]]

class RunnerLeaseTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_shared_lease_survives_hidden_pid_and_releases_on_process_death(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            lock = Path(temporary) / "runner.lock"
            code = (
                "from pathlib import Path\n"
                "import sys\n"
                "from autoswarm.platform import session_lease\n"
                "with session_lease(Path(sys.argv[1])):\n"
                " print('locked', flush=True)\n"
                " sys.stdin.read()\n"
            )
            process = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", code, str(lock)], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, **platform.detached_options())
            try:
                self.assertEqual(process.stdout.readline().strip(), "locked")
                handle = {"pid": process.pid, "identity": "hidden", "runner_lock": str(lock)}
                with patch("autoswarm.platform.identity", return_value=None):
                    self.assertTrue(platform.running(handle))
                    platform.stop_child(process)
                    process.wait()
                    self.assertFalse(platform.running(handle))
                self.assertTrue(lock.exists())  # A stale file alone is not liveness.
            finally:
                if process.poll() is None:
                    platform.stop_child(process)
                process.communicate()

        handle = {"pid": 123, "identity": "original"}

        with patch("autoswarm.platform.identity", return_value="reused"):

    def test_unavailable_lease_is_not_reported_as_lock_contention(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:

@unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "nt", "Windows process tree contracts")
class WindowsProcessTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def tree(self, exit_parent=False):
        # A Windows venv's python.exe redirects through another process. Use
        # the real interpreter so the fixture controls the parent it prints.
        python = getattr(sys, "_base_executable", sys.executable)
        code = ("import subprocess, sys\n"
                "child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(300)'])\n"
                "print(child.pid, flush=True)\n" + ("" if exit_parent else "sys.stdin.read()\n"))
        process = subprocess.Popen([python, "-c", code], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
        self.addCleanup(self.close_tree, process)
        child = int(process.stdout.readline())
        return process, child

    def close_tree(self, process):
        platform.stop_child(process)
        process.communicate(timeout=5)

    def test_stops_descendants_without_launching_taskkill(self):
        process, child = self.tree()
        with patch("autoswarm.platform.subprocess.run", side_effect=AssertionError("taskkill must not be used")):
            platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertIsNotNone(process.poll())
        self.assertIsNone(platform.identity(child))
        process.communicate(timeout=5)  # Descendants must release inherited pipes too.

    def test_exited_parent_does_not_leave_its_live_child(self):
        process, child = self.tree(exit_parent=True)
        process.wait(timeout=5)
        platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertIsNone(platform.identity(child))

    def test_rescans_for_children_missing_from_the_first_snapshot(self):
        from autoswarm import _winprocess
        process, child = self.tree()
        original = _winprocess._snapshot
        calls = []
        def snapshot(*args):
            cutoff, rows = original(*args)
            calls.append(True)
            return cutoff, [] if len(calls) == 1 else rows
        with patch.object(_winprocess, "_snapshot", side_effect=snapshot):
            platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(calls), 3)
        self.assertIsNone(platform.identity(child))

    def test_stops_multiple_generations_in_reversed_snapshot_order(self):
        from autoswarm import _winprocess
        branch_code = ("import subprocess, sys\n"
                       "child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(300)'])\n"
                       "print(child.pid, flush=True)\nsys.stdin.read()\n")
        code = ("import subprocess, sys\n"
                f"child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', {branch_code!r}], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)\n"
                "print(child.pid, child.stdout.readline().strip(), flush=True)\nsys.stdin.read()\n")
        python = getattr(sys, "_base_executable", sys.executable)
        process = subprocess.Popen([python, "-c", code], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
        self.addCleanup(self.close_tree, process)
        children = [int(value) for value in process.stdout.readline().split()]
        self.assertEqual(len(children), 2)
        original = _winprocess._snapshot
        def snapshot(*args):
            cutoff, rows = original(*args)
            return cutoff, list(reversed(rows))
        with patch.object(_winprocess, "_snapshot", side_effect=snapshot):
            platform.stop_child(process)
        for child in children:
            self.assertIsNone(platform.identity(child))
        process.communicate(timeout=5)

    def test_old_process_with_reused_parent_pid_is_not_terminated(self):
        from autoswarm import _winprocess
        sibling, _ = self.tree()
        process, child = self.tree()
        original = _winprocess._snapshot
        def snapshot(*args):
            cutoff, rows = original(*args)
            return cutoff, [(pid, process.pid if pid == sibling.pid else parent) for pid, parent in rows]
        with patch.object(_winprocess, "_snapshot", side_effect=snapshot):
            platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertIsNone(sibling.poll())
        self.assertIsNone(platform.identity(child))

    def test_pid_reused_after_snapshot_is_not_terminated(self):
        from autoswarm import _winprocess
        process, _ = self.tree()
        kernel, _ = _winprocess._api()
        cutoff_before_reuse = _winprocess._created(kernel, int(process._handle))
        sibling, _ = self.tree()
        original = _winprocess._snapshot
        calls = []
        def snapshot(*args):
            cutoff, rows = original(*args)
            calls.append(True)
            if len(calls) == 1:
                return cutoff_before_reuse, [(sibling.pid, process.pid)]
            return cutoff, rows
        with patch.object(_winprocess, "_snapshot", side_effect=snapshot):
            platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertIsNone(sibling.poll())

    def test_snapshot_failures_remain_errors(self):
        from autoswarm import _winprocess
        process, _ = self.tree()
        with patch.object(_winprocess, "_snapshot", side_effect=PermissionError("snapshot denied")):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(PermissionError, "snapshot denied"):
                platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertIsNone(process.poll())

    def test_concurrent_exit_access_denial_waits_for_completion(self):
        import ctypes
        from autoswarm import _winprocess
        process, child = self.tree()
        kernel, _ = _winprocess._api()
        terminate = kernel.TerminateProcess
        def concurrent_exit(handle, code):
            terminate(handle, code)
            ctypes.set_last_error(5)
            return 0
        with patch.object(kernel, "TerminateProcess", side_effect=concurrent_exit) as raced:
            platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertTrue(raced.called)
        self.assertIsNotNone(process.poll())
        self.assertIsNone(platform.identity(child))

    def test_other_termination_failures_remain_errors(self):
        import ctypes
        from autoswarm import _winprocess
        process, _ = self.tree()
        kernel, _ = _winprocess._api()
        def rejected(handle, code):
            ctypes.set_last_error(6)  # ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE
            return 0
        with patch.object(kernel, "TerminateProcess", side_effect=rejected):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError) as error:
                platform.stop_child(process)
        self.assertEqual(error.exception.winerror, 6)
        self.assertIsNone(process.poll())

class WebSocketPeer(socketserver.BaseRequestHandler):
    def exact(self, length):
        data = b""
        while len(data) < length:
            part = self.request.recv(length - len(data))
            if not part:
                raise EOFError()
            data += part
        return data

    def handle(self):
        self.request.settimeout(10)  # Bound the test harness only.
        try:
            header = b""
            while not header.endswith(b"\r\n\r\n"):
                header += self.exact(1)
            key = next(line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for line in header.decode().split("\r\n") if line.lower().startswith("sec-websocket-key:"))
            accept = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha1((key + "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11").encode()).digest()).decode()
            self.request.sendall(("HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Accept: " + accept + "\r\n\r\n").encode())
            while True:
                first, second = self.exact(2)
                length = second & 127
                if length == 126:
                    length = struct.unpack("!H", self.exact(2))[0]
                elif length == 127:
                    length = struct.unpack("!Q", self.exact(8))[0]
                mask = self.exact(4) if second & 128 else None
                body = self.exact(length)
                if mask:
                    body = bytes(value ^ mask[index % 4] for index, value in enumerate(body))
                message = json.loads(body)
                self.server.messages.append(message)
                if "id" not in message:
                    continue
                method, params = message["method"], message.get("params", {})
                error = None
                if method == "thread/read":
                    result = {"thread": {"id": "original", "status": {"type": self.server.status}}}
                elif method == "thread/turns/list":
                    result = {"data": [{"id": "active-turn", "status": "inProgress"}]}
                elif method == "turn/start":
                    result = {"turn": {"id": "continued-turn"}}
                elif method == "turn/steer":
                    if self.server.race:
                        self.server.race = False
                        self.server.status = "idle"
                        error = {"code": -32600, "message": "no active turn"}
                    else:
                        result = {"turnId": params["expectedTurnId"]}
                else:
                    result = {}
                response = {"id": message["id"], **({"error": error} if error else {"result": result})}
                body = json.dumps(response).encode()
                head = b"\x81" + (bytes([len(body)]) if len(body) < 126 else b"\x7e" + struct.pack("!H", len(body)))
                self.request.sendall(head + body)
        except (EOFError, ConnectionError, OSError):
            return


class HTTPPeer(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        self.server.requests.append((self.path, json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))))
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(json.dumps({"info": {"id": "parent-assistant-message", "role": "assistant"}, "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "continued"}]}).encode())

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

            nonlocal contested

            return acquire(path)

"""Exercise selection through real runners and native protocol peers."""
from __future__ import annotations

if __package__:

else:
    from autoswarm_test_support import cleanup_temporary

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures/provider.py"


class SelectionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.environment = patch.dict(os.environ, {"CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR": str(self.root / "native-cursor")})
        self.environment.start()
        self.records = Records(self.root / "state")
        self.config = {"providers": {name: {"command": [sys.executable, str(FIXTURE), name], **({"python": [sys.executable, str(FIXTURE), name]} if name == "nanobot" else {})} for name in BINARIES}}
        write_json(self.records.home / "config.json", self.config)

    def tearDown(self):
        for _, task in self.records.calls():
            engine.cancel(self.records, task["call_id"])
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10  # Test cleanup deadline only.
        while any(platform.running(read_json(path / "handle.json")) for path, _ in self.records.calls()):
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                self.fail("Fixture runner did not exit")
            time.sleep(.02)
        try:
            cleanup_temporary(self.tmp, deadline)
        finally:
            self.environment.stop()

    def run_child(self, provider, **kwargs):
        trace = self.root / (provider + ".jsonl")
        args = ["--selection-trace=" + str(trace), *kwargs.pop("provider_args", [])]
        call = engine.start_call(self.records, provider, "selection check", self.root, return_mode="wait", provider_args=args, **kwargs)
        result = engine.wait(self.records, [call["call_id"]])[0]
        return call, result, self.events(provider)

    def events(self, provider):
        return [json.loads(line) for line in (self.root / (provider + ".jsonl")).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()]

    def test_defaults_send_no_selection_controls(self):
        for provider in BINARIES:
            with self.subTest(provider=provider):
                call, result, events = self.run_child(provider)
                self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "completed", result)
                self.assertEqual(call["requested_selection"], {})
                self.assertFalse(any(event.get("method", "").startswith("session/set") for event in events))
                self.assertFalse({"--model", "--effort", "--reasoning-effort"}.intersection(events[0]["argv"]))
                for event in events:
                    params = event.get("params", {})
                    self.assertNotIn("model", params)
                    self.assertNotIn("effort", params)
                    self.assertNotIn("variant", params)
                self.assertFalse(any(event.get("path") in {"/config", "/agent", "/provider"} for event in events))

    def test_all_native_mappings_and_resume_preserve_explicit_choice(self):
        for provider in BINARIES:
            with self.subTest(provider=provider):
                model = "fixture/native-model" if provider == "opencode" else "native-model"
                call, result, events = self.run_child(provider, model=model, effort="deep-native", provider_args=["selection-catalog"])
                self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "completed", result)
                expected = {"model": model, "effort": "deep-native"}
                self.assertEqual(result["requested_selection"], expected)
                self.assertEqual(engine.inspect_call(self.records, call["call_id"])["requested_selection"], expected)
                argv = events[0]["argv"]
                if provider == "codex":
                    thread = next(event for event in events if event.get("method") == "thread/start")
                    turn = next(event for event in events if event.get("method") == "turn/start")
                    self.assertNotIn("effort", thread["params"])
                    self.assertEqual(turn["params"]["model"], model)
                    self.assertEqual(turn["params"]["effort"], "deep-native")
                elif provider == "opencode":
                    prompt = next(event for event in events if event.get("path", "").endswith("/message") and event["method"] == "POST")
                    self.assertEqual(prompt["params"]["model"], {"providerID": "fixture", "modelID": "native-model"})
                    self.assertEqual(prompt["params"]["variant"], "deep-native")
                elif provider == "claude-code":
                    self.assertEqual(argv[argv.index("--effort") + 1], "deep-native")
                elif provider == "muse":
                    methods = [event.get("method") for event in events]
                    self.assertLess(methods.index("session/setModel"), methods.index("session/setReasoningEffort"))
                    self.assertLess(methods.index("session/setReasoningEffort"), methods.index("turn/start"))
                    setting = next(event for event in events if event.get("method") == "session/setReasoningEffort")
                    self.assertEqual(setting["params"]["reasoningEffort"], "deep-native")
                elif provider == "grok":
                    self.assertEqual(argv[argv.index("--model") + 1], model)
                    self.assertEqual(argv[argv.index("--reasoning-effort") + 1], "deep-native")
                    self.assertFalse(any(event.get("method", "").startswith("session/set") for event in events))
                elif provider == "cursor":
                    init = next(event for event in events if event.get("method") == "initialize")
                    self.assertTrue(init["params"]["clientCapabilities"]["_meta"]["parameterizedModelPicker"])
                    setting = next(event for event in events if event.get("method") == "session/set_config_option" and event["params"]["configId"] == "reasoning")
                    self.assertEqual(setting["params"]["value"], "deep-native")
                else:
                    setting = next(event for event in events if event.get("method") == "session/set_config_option" and event["params"]["configId"] == "thought_level")
                    self.assertEqual(setting["params"]["value"], "deep-native")
                    if provider == "copilot":
                        self.assertEqual(argv[argv.index("--reasoning-effort") + 1], "deep-native")
                continued = engine.resume(self.records, call["call_id"], "follow up", return_mode="wait")
                resumed = engine.wait(self.records, [continued["call_id"]])[0]
                self.assertEqual(resumed["outcome"], "completed", resumed)
                self.assertEqual(resumed["requested_selection"], expected)
                self.assertEqual(resumed["native_session_id"], result["native_session_id"])
                override = engine.resume(self.records, continued["call_id"], "change effort", effort="light-native", return_mode="wait")
                changed = engine.wait(self.records, [override["call_id"]])[0]
                self.assertEqual(changed["outcome"], "completed", changed)
                self.assertEqual(changed["requested_selection"], {"model": model, "effort": "light-native"})
                self.assertEqual(read_json(self.records.call(call["call_id"]) / "result.json"), result)
